articles.title: Stealth frigate INS Trishul takes part in bilateral naval exercise 'Varuna' in France
articles.summary: The Indian Navy's stealth frigate INS Trishul recently participated in the flagship bilateral naval exercise 'Varuna' in France. This drill is crucial for strengthening maritime ties and professional bonds between India and France. Such international exercises enhance interoperability and regional security, providing SSB aspirants valuable insights into joint naval operations and defence diplomacy.

articles.title: Explosions heard in Ethiopia's capital after drone flights banned
articles.summary: Explosions rocked Ethiopia's capital overnight, with sounds reported near the military headquarters in the west and another area in the south of the city. Residents and diplomatic sources confirmed hearing the blasts. This incident, targeting areas close to critical security infrastructure, indicates potential internal instability or a security challenge within the nation's capital.

articles.title: Can Malik Willis' legs help Dolphins overcome loss of De'Von Achane?
articles.summary: Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis has emerged as a formidable rushing threat, accumulating 101 yards. This unusual dual-threat role for a QB is proving challenging for opposing defenses and even surprising for his own team's veterans. His performance highlights a shift in quarterback play, adding a dynamic new dimension to the Dolphins' offensive strategy.

articles.title: Why Lac La Biche's shoreline is getting a health checkup
articles.summary: A team of biologists from Masse Environmental, contracted by Living Lakes Canada, is meticulously studying Lac La Biche's shoreline to analyze environmental changes over the past decade. From a boat, they are assessing shifts in the lake's ecology. This vital research underscores the importance of continuous environmental monitoring for safeguarding freshwater ecosystems and informing future conservation strategies.

articles.title: Turkey says it will block Greece-Cyprus cable work on its continental shelf
articles.summary: Turkey's Defence Ministry objects to a planned electricity link between Greece and Cyprus, asserting it won't allow unauthorized activity on its continental shelf. This move highlights Ankara's long-standing territorial and maritime boundary disputes with Greece in the eastern Mediterranean. This geopolitical tension over sovereignty and resource access is crucial for understanding international defence dynamics.
